Rules / Maintainability

SK7020 Duplicated block

A run of at least minTokens tokens that occurs identically, up to identifier and literal names, somewhere else in the repository. The file's extern alias, using and namespace header is not part of the run.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitywarning
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.8

Why

Duplication is the one SonarQube feature with no Roslyn equivalent, and the AI workflow needs it more than most: agents copy-paste by nature, and a block pasted four times is four places a fix has to land. Detection is token-level type-2 clone detection — identifiers and literals normalised to a class, keywords and punctuation kept exact — so a block copied and renamed is still found, which is the copy people actually make. A clone group is reported once, at its first occurrence, with the rest as related locations; reporting it at every occurrence would turn one problem into n findings and make the count meaningless.

Example

Instead of:

// the same 100-token block, pasted into four files with the variables renamed

Write:

// one method, called four times

When it does not fire

Not a false-positive-prone rule in the usual sense — a reported group either is or is not a token-for-token match, and the match is verified exactly rather than trusted from the rolling hash, so a hash collision cannot produce a finding. What it can do is report duplication that is deliberate, or duplication nobody wrote. Four exclusions handle the cases that matter and are the whole of the rule's tuning: generated files are excluded from the findings and from both halves of the percentage; the file header — extern alias and using directives, and each namespace declaration's keyword and name — is skipped before hashing, and the lines it occupies leave both halves too; test files are measured but counted and reported separately, because duplication in tests is often the readable choice and gating it drives people to write worse tests; and the 100-token default is Sonar's own for C#, which is roughly 25 lines. ⚠ The header exclusion is decided by syntax node, not by the word using: a using statement or declaration inside a method body is resource management, is real code, and counts in full. ⚠ And that last figure is not above the length of all boilerplate, which this rule used to claim: identifiers normalise to one class, so using A.B.C; and using D.E.F; are the same nine tokens, and measured over 289 analyzer files the header alone was a median 62 of the 100-token window with Roslyn's mandated declaration shape another 45 — two analyzers were a clone of each other before either had done anything. Skipping the header took Skala's own repository from 12.7 % to 6.8 % without one line of logic moving.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7020.severity
  • dotnet_code_quality.SK7020.minTokens (default 100)
